intro: Hi again! You can already count to 20 — today we go all the way to 100 and use numbers in real life: your age, your phone number and prices in rupiah. Warm-up: how do you say 20 in English?
teachingNotes: Stress is the whole difference between -teen and -ty: thirTEEN (13), fourTEEN (14) vs THIRty (30), FORty (40). Learners say them the same way — exaggerate the stress and teach the check question 'One-three or three-zero?'.
Spelling: forty has no u (four → forty), and 21–99 take a hyphen in writing (twenty-one, fifty-six). 100 = one hundred or a hundred.
Age uses be, not have: 'I'm 25 (years old)'. Never 'I have 25 years (old)'. 'I'm 25 years' without 'old' is not natural — teach 'I'm 25' or 'I'm 25 years old'. Ask with 'How old are you?'.

Phone numbers are read one digit at a time in small groups with pauses (0812 5567 3490 = oh-eight-one-two, five-five-six-seven, three-four-nine-oh). 0 = 'oh' or 'zero'; 'double five' for 55 is optional. Never read them as big numbers.

Prices: after a number, thousand and hundred never take -s (twenty-five thousand, not 'twenty-five thousands'), and rupiah has no -s. English writes 25,000 with a comma where Indonesian writes 25.000 with a dot. Chunks: 'How much is it?' — 'It's 25,000 rupiah.'
Limits: stay at or below a hundred thousand rupiah; no millions, decimals or years. Grammar only through fixed chunks (I'm…, My number is…, It's…, How much is it?); no past tense.

keyPoints.title: Numbers 21–100
keyPoints.explanation: The tens end in -ty: twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, then one hundred. For 21–99 say the ten, then the unit, with a hyphen in writing. -teen numbers have stress at the end (thirTEEN), -ty numbers at the start (THIRty).

keyPoints.title: Your age and phone number
keyPoints.explanation: For age, say I'm + the number, and add years old if you like. Don't use have. Read phone numbers one digit at a time, in small groups; 0 is 'oh' or 'zero'.

keyPoints.title: Prices in rupiah
keyPoints.explanation: Say how many thousand, then 'thousand rupiah'. After a number, thousand and hundred have no -s. English writes 25,000 with a comma; Indonesian writes 25.000 with a dot.

examples.en: How much is it? — It's 25,000 rupiah.
3,500 rupiah = three thousand five hundred rupiah

guidedPractice.hint: -ty numbers have the stress at the start; -teen numbers at the end.

assessment.rubric: Correct: forty-seven (with or without the hyphen). 'fourty-seven' = 70 (spelling). 'fourteen'/'seventy-four' = 0.

Say it in English: Umur saya 32 tahun.

assessment.prompt: Listen. Write the phone number you hear (digits only).

assessment.listen: The coffee is eighteen thousand rupiah.

blocks.text: You already know 1–20. Now learn the **tens** — they all end in **-ty**. For the numbers in between, say the ten and then the unit: **twenty-one, twenty-two … ninety-nine**. In writing, use a hyphen: *forty-six*. After ninety-nine comes **one hundred** (or **a hundred**).

id.text: Kamu sudah tahu 1–20. Sekarang pelajari **puluhan** — semuanya berakhiran **-ty**. Untuk angka di antaranya, sebut puluhannya lalu satuannya: **twenty-one, twenty-two … ninety-nine**. Saat menulis, pakai tanda hubung: *forty-six*. Setelah ninety-nine ada **one hundred** (atau **a hundred**).

rows.id: dua puluh satu · lima puluh enam · sembilan puluh sembilan

blocks.text: **thirteen or thirty?** The -teen numbers have the stress at the end: thir**TEEN**, fif**TEEN**. The -ty numbers have the stress at the start: **THIR**ty, **FIF**ty. Not sure what you heard? Ask: *One-three or three-zero?*

id.text: **thirteen atau thirty?** Angka -teen ditekan di akhir: thir**TEEN**, fif**TEEN**. Angka -ty ditekan di awal: **THIR**ty, **FIF**ty. Ragu dengan yang kamu dengar? Tanyakan: *One-three or three-zero?*

blocks.prompt: How do you write 40 in words?
blocks.explain: 40 is forty — no u, even though 4 is four. Fourteen is 14.

id.explain: 40 adalah forty — tanpa u, walaupun 4 ditulis four. Fourteen itu 14.

blocks.text: To give your age, say **I'm** + the number. You can add **years old**: *I'm 25* or *I'm 25 years old*. Don't say *I have 25 years* — English uses **am / is** for age, not *have*. To ask someone, say **How old are you?**

id.text: Untuk menyebut umur, katakan **I'm** + angkanya. Boleh ditambah **years old**: *I'm 25* atau *I'm 25 years old*. Jangan bilang *I have 25 years* — bahasa Inggris memakai **am / is** untuk umur, bukan *have*. Untuk bertanya, katakan **How old are you?**

blocks.text: Read a phone number **one digit at a time**, in small groups with a short pause between them. Say 0 as **oh** or **zero**. Two same digits together can be **double**: 55 = *double five*.

id.text: Baca nomor telepon **satu angka demi satu angka**, dalam kelompok kecil dengan jeda singkat di antaranya. Angka 0 dibaca **oh** atau **zero**. Dua angka sama berurutan boleh dibaca **double**: 55 = *double five*.

blocks.prompt: Choose the right answer to: How old are you?
blocks.explain: Age uses I'm (I am), not I have. 'My age 19' has no verb.

id.explain: Umur memakai I'm (I am), bukan I have. 'My age 19' tidak punya kata kerja.

blocks.text: Rupiah prices are big numbers, but they're easy: say how many **thousand**, then **rupiah**. *Rp25.000* = **twenty-five thousand rupiah** (dua puluh lima *ribu*). With hundreds: *Rp2.500* = **two thousand five hundred rupiah**. To ask the price, say **How much is it?** — **It's 15,000 rupiah.**

id.text: Harga dalam rupiah memang angka besar, tapi mudah: sebut berapa **thousand** (ribu), lalu **rupiah**. *Rp25.000* = **twenty-five thousand rupiah** (dua puluh lima *ribu*). Dengan ratusan: *Rp2.500* = **two thousand five hundred rupiah**. Untuk menanyakan harga, katakan **How much is it?** — **It's 15,000 rupiah.**

rows.note: a hundred thousand / one hundred thousand rupiah

blocks.text: Two common mistakes: after a number, **thousand** and **hundred** never take -s (*twenty-five thousand*, not *twenty-five thousands*), and **rupiah** has no -s either. Also, English writes **25,000** with a **comma**, while Indonesian writes **25.000** with a dot.

id.text: Dua kesalahan umum: setelah angka, **thousand** dan **hundred** tidak pernah diberi -s (*twenty-five thousand*, bukan *twenty-five thousands*), dan **rupiah** juga tanpa -s. Selain itu, bahasa Inggris menulis **25,000** dengan **koma**, sedangkan bahasa Indonesia menulis **25.000** dengan titik.

blocks.explain: After a number, thousand has no -s: forty-five thousand rupiah.

id.explain: Setelah angka, thousand tidak diberi -s: forty-five thousand rupiah.

material.title: At the warung and on the road

blocks.text: When you shop or travel, numbers are everywhere: prices, room numbers, bus numbers, phone numbers. Listen carefully, and **repeat the number back** to check it. Even native speakers do this all the time.

id.text: Saat belanja atau bepergian, angka ada di mana-mana: harga, nomor kamar, nomor bus, nomor telepon. Dengarkan baik-baik, lalu **ulangi angkanya** untuk memastikan. Penutur asli pun selalu melakukannya.

rows.en: How much is the nasi goreng? — It's 22,000 rupiah.

rows.id: Maaf, lima belas atau lima puluh?

blocks.text: Check a phone number by reading it back in groups: *Oh-eight-one-two … five-five-six-seven?* If one digit is wrong, the other person can fix it quickly.

id.text: Pastikan nomor telepon dengan membacanya ulang per kelompok: *Oh-eight-one-two … five-five-six-seven?* Kalau ada satu angka yang salah, lawan bicara bisa langsung membetulkannya.

suggestedQuestions: How can I hear the difference between thirteen and thirty?
Do I say 'oh' or 'zero' in phone numbers?
Why is it 'twenty thousand' and not 'twenty thousands'?
How do I ask how much something is?
